clue.text: Topping paper (does this ring a'bell ?).

parts.note: a jester's hat with bells is a topping, and the same two words name a large size of writing paper

explanation.surface: A question about some excellent stationery, asking whether it sounds familiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' reads as 'excellent' but is a hat; the jester's cap hung with bells gave its name (and watermark) to a large paper size.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British paper size, about 13 by 16 inches, named after the jester's-cap watermark once used on it.

clue.text: Letter shows Greek love of tennis'?

definitions.text: Letter shows Greek love of tennis'?

parts.words: Letter shows Greek love of tennis'?
parts.note: in tennis a zero score, love, is O, and the Greek alphabet's short O is the letter meant

explanation.surface: A letter reveals that a Greek is fond of tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' looks like affection; in tennis scoring it means nil, the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a short O.

clue.text: Dr Johnson called them the pedigree of nations

definitions.text: Dr Johnson called them the pedigree of nations

parts.words: Dr Johnson called them the pedigree of nations
parts.note: Samuel Johnson said tongues of speech show where peoples descend from

explanation.surface: A quotation from Samuel Johnson about what traces a people's ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnson, the dictionary maker, wrote 'Languages are the pedigree of nations'.
explanation.definitionFit: Systems of speech used by peoples, such as French or Welsh.

clue.text: Provides no support for future butterflies

indicators.note: no support means the supporting word is removed from the larvae

parts.note: caterpillars grow into butterflies
pillars support a building

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to back plans for butterflies to come.
explanation.walkthrough: CATERPILLARS loses PILLARS, leaving CATER + S.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplying food or what is needed is to furnish it.

clue.text: Sent with' a view to support credit a/c changes

indicators.note: changes means these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a/c is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Bookkeeping jargon about credit and account adjustments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a/c' supplies AC; with SUPPORT and CREDIT the fifteen letters are anagrammed, as 'changes' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday card bearing a scenic photograph, posted home.

clue.text: The' non-drinker is improved with a drink all round

indicators.note: a drink placed all round something means its letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: beer is a drink
TT, teetotal, marks someone who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: An abstainer seems to have been made better by a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The non-drinker' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is the teetotaller, enclosed as 'all round' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improved has become superior to what it was.

clue.text: Criminal for whom double- Dutch has some meaning?.

definitions.text: Criminal for whom double- Dutch has some meaning?.

parts.words: Criminal for whom double- Dutch has some meaning?.
parts.note: in Cockney slang a 'Dutch' is a wife, so a double one is two wives at once

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker who can make sense of gibberish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double Dutch' means gibberish; 'Dutch' is old slang for a wife (from 'duchess'), so two wives.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who marries while already married, a crime in Britain.

clue.text: Port of Lebanon or of Libya

explanation.surface: A harbour city in either of two Mediterranean countries.
explanation.definitionFit: One city of this name is a harbour town in northern Lebanon; another is the capital and seaport of Libya.

clue.text: Russia's lightning variety of apple?

parts.note: red is the traditional colour of Soviet Russia
a streak of lightning

explanation.surface: Russia's fast new apple cultivar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russia's' gives RED (communist), and STREAK is a flash of lightning.
explanation.definitionFit: An old English cider apple cultivar with red-striped skin.

clue.text: Tennyson did not envy Finch born as a 10 …

definitions.text: Tennyson did not envy Finch born as a 10

parts.words: Tennyson did not envy Finch born as a 10
parts.note: In Memoriam says 'I envy not ... the [finch] born within the cage', and 10 across is that caged bird

explanation.surface: A literary note on a poet's feelings about a small songbird kept captive.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's In Memoriam (canto 27) begins 'I envy not in any moods / The captive void of noble rage, / The linnet born within the cage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown finch, long kept as a song bird.

clue.text: . while Blake's Robin as this enraged all heaven

definitions.text: while Blake's Robin as this enraged all heaven

parts.words: while Blake's Robin as this enraged all heaven
parts.note: Blake's Auguries of Innocence says a robin redbreast kept captive 'puts all Heaven in a Rage'

explanation.surface: Continuing the poetry theme: a poet's robin whose captivity angered heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: Blake wrote 'A Robin Redbreast in a Cage / Puts all Heaven in a Rage'; the clue continues from 9 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbird kept in confinement as a pet, as the robin is in Blake's couplet.

clue.text: Was-this what Herrick heard when Julia went ?

definitions.text: Was-this what Herrick heard when Julia went ?

parts.words: Was-this what Herrick heard when Julia went ?
parts.note: Herrick's poem 'Upon Julia's Clothes' has Julia going 'in silks', whose swish is the sound meant

explanation.surface: A question about the sound a poet noticed as his beloved walked past.
explanation.walkthrough: Herrick: 'Whenas in silks my Julia goes'. The rustle of silk skirts as a woman moves is the word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustling of silk dresses, by extension frilly showiness.

clue.text: His charges will never forget him

definitions.text: His charges will never forget him

parts.words: His charges will never forget him
parts.note: elephants are said never to forget, and they are the charges of an Indian elephant keeper

explanation.surface: A tribute to someone whose pupils or wards will always remember him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' suggests pupils or clients; here they are elephants, proverbially unforgetting.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant driver or keeper in India and South-East Asia.

clue.text: Obstacles to taking a horse on board ?

indicators.note: the ship letters are taking the horse in, so they enclose it

parts.note: on board suggests a steamship, abbreviated SS
a nag is a horse, usually an old one

explanation.surface: A query about the difficulties of loading a horse onto a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention for being inside the ship abbreviation; 'taking' says the ship holds the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Snags are hitches or unforeseen difficulties.

clue.text: So shaped his parcel is awkward to wrap

indicators.note: awkward signals the letters are put into an untidy new order

explanation.surface: A round package is hard to wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' anagrams HIS PARCEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Round like a ball, which is why the package resists paper.

clue.text: Disturbing events one is acutely aware of

indicators.note: disturbing these letters throws them into a new arrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Upsetting happenings that someone feels very keenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbing' looks like an adjective describing the events; it is the anagram signal on EVENTS + I + IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keenly responsive to something is what being highly perceptive of it means.

clue.text: Vessel for liquor, and the bird, do we hear, to draw it?

indicators.note: do we hear means the phrase is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to tap a cask is to draw liquor from it
a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: A drinking vessel and a bird, with a query about extracting liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: A tappit hen is a large Scottish pewter drinking measure with a lid; 'tap it' said aloud gives TAPPIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish lidded tankard for ale or claret.

clue.text: Declared by a journalist about the lock-up

indicators.note: a and the journalist go about the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A reporter's statement concerning the jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock-up' looks like a prison but splits into 'lock' and 'up'; 'up' turns the lock round in this down clue, and 'about' puts the journalist pair around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated firmly, a synonym of proclaimed.

clue.text: Forgery afoot ?

parts.note: not fraud under way, but a thing made in a blacksmith's forge and fixed to a hoof

explanation.surface: A hint that some counterfeiting is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forgery' means the product of a forge, and 'afoot' means on a horse's foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved iron plate a farrier forges and nails to a hoof.

clue.text: Covering say a seance phenomenon

indicators.note: say signals the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: wrapping is a covering

explanation.surface: Wrapping as an example of something that happens at a seance.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirits supposedly communicate at seances by knocking sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking noises attributed to spirits at seances.

clue.text: A spot of blubber

explanation.surface: A small amount of whale fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny mark or dot; also an old word for the fat of whales or seals.

clue.text: Sugar Co's wild animals

indicators.note: wild means these letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A sugar company's untamed beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild animals' reads as one phrase, but 'wild' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Big American cats, also called pumas or mountain lions.

clue.text: A jolly girl for the Fleet

parts.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cheerful young woman joining the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective but is the old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A great fleet of warships, like the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: How one might fret about a tree

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the pine is a tree

explanation.surface: Wondering how someone might worry over a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How one might' is a link that turns the clue into a question about worrying over a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To complain or be discontented, a synonym of worrying.

clue.text: Schooldays in the States are the limit

parts.note: a school term is a stretch of schooldays
the US, United States

explanation.surface: An American remark that schooldays are unbearable.
explanation.walkthrough: TERM + IN + US. 'the limit' is the definition, not part of the American picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The end point or boundary, as a railway line's final station is.

clue.text: A teach-in arranged for, brewers ?

definitions.note: the definition names what brewers of a pot make, a noun beside a phrase

indicators.note: arranged means these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone organises a seminar for people in the beer business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewers' suggests beer makers, but they are people brewing a pot of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea from China, something one brews in a pot.

clue.text: Stone tree-god.

parts.note: the ash is a tree
a lar is a Roman household god

explanation.surface: A deity of trees carved from stone.
explanation.walkthrough: LAR, plural LARES, is a Roman household god.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed, square-cut masonry blocks used in building.

clue.text: Inscription of Montrose, or Sleepy .Hollow

explanation.surface: A carved message from a Scottish town or an American village.
explanation.definitionFit: The writing on a coin or medal; and the title word of Scott's A Legend of Montrose and Irving's The Legend of Sleepy Hollow.

clue.text: Find trouble when a gin is mixed, in what the doctor ordered

indicators.note: in places the mixed letters inside the medicine

parts.note: a dose is what a doctor prescribes

indicators.note: mixed means these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescription has a gin cocktail in it, which spells trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' scrambles A GIN into IAGN, and 'in' puts that inside the prescription; 'trouble' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify an illness or fault from its symptoms is to pinpoint the problem.
